- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp spike or reversal, adjust for lagged reaction — model often underreacts to sentiment-driven volatility.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (e.g., 0.88+), model frequently overshoots and continues rising; apply early correction by reducing forecast slope after peak sentiment.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add downward bias or reduce upward momentum.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a peak, model often fails to anticipate — apply downward bias in next forecast if sentiment is still high.
- Model tends to overestimate early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is rising — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days if sentiment >0.6.
- If sentiment history shows repeated high-low oscillation, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply smoothing or dampening to forecast curve.
